    - heading "Accessibility" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: A real <input> with a <label> tied to it – works with forms, autofill, password managers and screen readers
      - listitem: The hint and the error are linked with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid and is announced politely when it appears
      - listitem: Clear, show password and copy are labelled buttons; the reveal button reports its state with aria-pressed and "Copied" is announced
      - listitem: Without a label, a text placeholder becomes the field's accessible name – better still, pass aria-label
      - listitem: Focus darkens the edge a step – no ring, the caret shows where you are; the buttons get a clear outline under keyboard focus. Need a stronger focus edge? Override --ui-tf(c)-edge-focus / --ui-tfc-shadow-focus
      - listitem: dir="auto" on the value and the message, so Arabic or Hebrew text reads the right way in any form; prefix, suffix and buttons follow the page direction
    - heading "Motion" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: "No focus ring: the hairline edge firms up on hover and a little more on focus"
      - listitem: An error nudges the field once and its message slides in out of a short blur, in place of the hint – nothing below moves
      - listitem: Showing a password brings the characters out of a short blur; the copy icon morphs into a check that draws itself
      - listitem: With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
    - heading "Responsive behavior" [level=2]
    - list:
      - listitem: Fills its container; long values, prefixes and messages never push it wider – a long prefix is cut at its start, so the part next to the value stays
      - listitem: On touch screens the field grows to a comfortable tap height, its buttons to 32px with a larger hit area, and it uses 16px text, so iOS doesn't zoom in on focus
      - listitem: "Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme=\"dark\""
